decisions.reason: As a software product with visible prior commitment and very strong alignment to the firm's connected, data-driven infrastructure strategy, management is likely to justify past investment and continue unless results clearly deteriorate.

Although less central to the firm's digital future than the software and control products, it builds on the established infrastructure offer and had its own page, so management would still tend to retain it rather than admit a mistaken launch.

Control technology is close to the core business and supports more connected operation of water-engineering assets, so sunk development effort and strategic fit favor continuation despite only moderate public visibility.

This newer automation and system software offer sits squarely in the firm's announced web-based and data-driven direction and was presented prominently, making management especially likely to persist with it.
